title: Loss Function
body:
[[Log Loss]]
[[Vector Norm]]

A regression loss is a [[Vector Norm]] of the residual vector: $L_2$ squared is mean squared
error, $L_1$ is mean absolute error. [[Log Loss]] and [[Cross-Entropy Loss]] are the
classification alternatives and are not norms. See [[LINEAR ALGEBRA FOR DATA SCIENCE]].

A loss is minimised **in expectation** over the data distribution, which is what "expected risk"
means; see [[Random Variable]] in [[STATISTICS]] (MATH 2234). Minimising squared error is exactly
what [[Linear Regression]] does.

The loss is the objective in an [[Optimization]] problem, which is why it has to be differentiable:
[[Gradient Descent]] needs a slope to follow. Accuracy is the thing you actually care about and is
not usable as a loss for exactly that reason, since it is flat almost everywhere.
